source: human-verified pending: drafted by Claude from the code, to be reviewed by the owner

flaws.title: Passwords are stored as unsalted MD5
flaws.why: hashPassword uses createHash("md5") with no salt and no work factor, so a leaked users table is cracked in minutes and equal passwords share a hash.

flaws.title: No limit on failed sign-in attempts
flaws.why: login returns 401 on a wrong password and counts nothing, so an attacker can guess passwords for any email without lockout or delay.

flaws.title: Sessions never expire
flaws.why: openSession stores only { token, userId } and userOf accepts any stored token forever, so a stolen token works for good.

flaws.title: No way to sign out or revoke a session
flaws.why: The sessions store has only insert and findByToken; there is no delete, so a user cannot sign out and a leaked token cannot be revoked.

flaws.title: Password hash compared with a non-constant-time check
flaws.why: user.passwordHash !== hashPassword(password) uses an ordinary string compare instead of timingSafeEqual; the timing leak is small but a careful reviewer flags it.
